review_method: Independent visual inspection of the original PONT map page, legend, scale and each complete water region; every complete source and baseline ring was viewed and independently decoded. The regional comparison is geographic and visual, not a numerical shoreline registration. Present public validation checks included files only.
counted_unit: Distinct logical inventory target IDs; not a count of distinct named waterbodies or verified names.
cumulative_count_scope: Recorded fresh-research inventory targets including unresolved scope holds and access gaps, not verified scalar names. Only prior51 membership/follow-up flags, existing published eastern-basin scope wording and current3 delta were checked; prior original-source and geometry judgments were not reaudited.

inherited_scope_continuity.scope: Inherited r16 result supports only a generalized Sandfly Lake association for the selected eastern basin; it does not equate that feature with the entire named lake or extend the name to connecting river water.
inherited_scope_continuity.supported_name_scope: The complete eastern basin corresponds at regional scale to water beneath the Lake part of the Sandfly Lake label. Its broad northern cap, western notch, eastern indentation and lower eastward arm taper into the southern tip. The full outline was compared with mapped water and surrounding shore. This supports generalized Sandfly Lake association for the selected feature, not equivalence with the entire named lake or extension of that name to connecting river water.

findings.supported_name_scope: The entire north-south outline corresponds geographically to mapped water between Struga, Ohrid and Pogradec. Its broad northern cap, northeast shoulder, long east and west sides and rounded southern end were compared. Lake Ohrid is a low-confidence geographic naming candidate from literal wording within a partial conservation overlay, qualified by re-designate. Strong shape correspondence does not establish name coverage or naming authority for the complete selected water polygon. No supported whole-water identity or protected-site/water-boundary equivalence is assigned.
limits: The literal Lake Ohrid wording is a low-confidence geographic candidate only. Its conservation-overlay context does not directly establish naming coverage across the complete water polygon.
PONT is a conservation trust/fund, not a government naming registry. One thematic map and geographic correspondence do not establish independent naming authority or an official waterbody identity.

Protected-site outlines, hatch lines and international borders are not shorelines or exact name boundaries. No exact named-water extent, scalar product name, Korean form or geometry repair is approved.
